newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador president keeps defense, foreign ministers.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador president keeps defense, foreign ministers.

text.p: Ecuador's President Fabian Alarcon has so far confirmed he is keeping Defense Minister General Ramiro Ricaurte and Foreign Minister Jose Ayala in his cabinet after Sunday's referendum.
"He (the president) has confirmed his confidence in me," Ricaurte told journalists at a press conference Wednesday.
Meanwhile, an official at the foreign ministry told Reuters that Ayala had only offered to resign "out of politeness, but he will be maintained firmly at the head of Ecuador's diplomacy."
Alarcon decided to reshuffle his cabinet after a referendum Sunday in which voters endorsed his interim presidency and approved the removal of former President Abdala Bucaram by Congress.

Several members of the 16-strong cabinet offered their resignations after the vote as a gesture of good will to give Alarcon a free hand in choosing ministers after the democratic approval of his administration.
The head of the central bank, Fidel Jaramillo, offered his resignation as well Tuesday night.
No word has yet been received on Jaramillo's tenure.
According to press reports Wednesday, the president said he would keep Cesar Verduga as government minister and Mario Jaramillo as education minister.
The only cabinet member so far known to be leaving his post is Administration Secretary Arturo Gangotena.
Alarcon, who was nominated to act as interim president by Congress after Bucaram's ousting, is expected to complete the cabinet reshuffle by the end of this week.
Alarcon will serve until August 1998, when a new president will take over after general elections.
